summary.en: British admiral commanding the allied fleet at Navarino in 1827. He had orders to enforce an armistice without fighting, and destroyed the Ottoman and Egyptian fleet in an afternoon.

body_html.en:
Codrington had commanded a ship of the line at Trafalgar. In 1827 he was senior officer of the British, French and Russian squadrons sent to impose the mediation agreed in the Treaty of London on the Sultan and on Ibrahim Pasha.

He led the combined fleet into Navarino Bay on 20 October to make the point that the blockade was real. A shot fired at a British boat became a general engagement, and by evening most of the Ottoman and Egyptian fleet had been sunk or burnt. London called it an "untoward event" and recalled him the following year. Greece gave him a street and a statue.
